entries.place: The gates of the Redmist Estate
entries.what_happened: Carla introduced herself to Julian as his bodyguard, inside the Redmist Estate and wherever else he went, and said his safety was her top priority. She asked to borrow his phone. Julian asked why before handing it over. Carla explained she wanted to check location sharing, unfamiliar apps with access, and cloud auto-upload, saying she did not care about his messages. The gate intercom announced the household assembled in the east parlor awaiting the new master. Julian gave her the phone for two minutes and asked about the east parlor. Carla said it was in the main building, second floor, end of the gallery hall. She turned off location, removed location access from two third-party apps, and killed cloud sync, returning the phone in under two minutes. She told him to look like he owned the place. The gates swung open and a maid waited on the steps.

entries.place: The gravel drive and front steps of the Redmist mansion
entries.what_happened: Julian repeated the directions to the east parlor and asked Carla how the household expected to be greeted, saying he had never had staff. Carla advised him to say what he meant, not to thank them for doing their jobs, and to use their names back when they introduced themselves. Julian walked up the gravel drive toward the maid. She descended two steps and bowed shallowly, introducing herself as Lisette, his personal maid, and said the household was assembled in the east parlor. She glanced at Carla without expression, then led them up the steps into a high-ceilinged hall smelling of beeswax and cut flowers.

entries.place: The east parlor of the Redmist mansion
others: the older man who kept the estate's vehicles
entries.what_happened: Lisette led Julian and Carla through the portrait-lined gallery hall into the east parlor, where the staff stood in a semicircle near the hearth and a silver tea service waited. Gabriella Redmist, apart from the others in a burgundy dress and pearls, came forward with both hands and welcomed Julian, saying they had a lot to talk about but the staff should have their moment first. Julian thanked her, said the will had left him in the dark about the household, and suggested they talk after introductions. Gabriella seated herself in a wingback chair by the hearth. Lisette introduced Louise Marchand as the chef, then the gardener and the older man who kept the estate's vehicles. Lisette said tea was poured and Louise had made pastries. Julian thanked Louise plainly, told the staff he had not known his grandfather and would not pretend otherwise, and asked them to tell him plainly if they could not do something rather than let it go quiet and wrong. He asked Lisette to walk him through the whole house after the tea. Louise smiled, pleased. The staff dispersed to errands. Gabriella rose and said she wanted a word before the evening, that her rooms were in the guest wing, and that Julian should see his grandfather's third-floor study before deciding anything. She brushed his arm with her sleeve and left.

entries.place: The east parlor of the Redmist mansion
entries.what_happened: Julian set down his cup and said they would start with the third-floor study, since his grandfather had wanted him to see it before anything colored his thinking. He asked Lisette whether anything in the house was off-limits. Lisette said nothing was formally off-limits to him because he owned the house, but that there were rooms she would not have shown a guest and rooms where the staff kept to their work. She said the study had been closed since the funeral, with dust sheets, and that Mr. Bernard's private papers were as he left them. She pointed out the lift on the far side of the hall and the main stair at the north corner, saying it was a long climb either way. Carla drifted toward the stairwell, watching the gallery portraits.

entries.place: The north stair and the third-floor study of the Redmist mansion
entries.what_happened: Julian chose the stairs to learn the house as everyone else moved through it. On the climb he asked Carla, quietly, whether she had ever been up to the third-floor study. Carla said she had been at Bernard's shoulder for six years and could count on one hand the times he took her to the study; he went up alone most nights, sometimes with Jezebel, the money woman, and never told her what went on there. She said whatever was in the room was the real thing, because he did not keep trophies. At the top, Julian said he had never met the man and was supposed to read his mind from a room, then asked Carla to help pull off the dust sheets. Carla pushed the door open and began removing sheets, warning him papers were everywhere on the floor. The long, narrow room had shuttered windows, a cold fireplace, a tall bookcase, and a heavy oak desk with one center drawer. On the desk, weighted under a brass paperknife, sat a single sheet of paper set apart from the rest.

entries.place: The third-floor study of the Redmist mansion
entries.what_happened: Julian read the weighted sheet without touching it, noting it had been left there deliberately. The letter, in cramped handwriting signed B.R., said that if he was reading it the writer was dead and Julian was the one he had chosen; that he had searched for Julian for years and would not apologize for his mother's choice; that the money and house were not a gift but a debt now Julian's; that he trusted the house's ledgers more than any face in the city and that Jezebel kept them honestly, if she still lived; and that Julian should not trust anyone who claimed to know what he wanted, as he had told only Julian, in that room. Below, in different, shakier ink, a line said the third drawer held it and the brass key was under the blotter. Julian told Carla the shaky hand might be the last thing Bernard wrote and asked her to clear the room before he pulled drawers. Carla checked the third drawer's face and seam, found nothing jammed and no wire, and lifted the blotter to reveal a small brass key green at the edges. She told him to open it slowly and keep his hand out of the dark once the wood was clear, and to stop if it caught. Julian took the key, crouched, inserted it in the third drawer's lock, and turned it slowly while keeping his free hand clear.
